title: Crêpes
subtitle: French thin pancakes, sweet or savoury
excerpt: Wafer-thin French pancakes made from a rested batter, cooked in a hot buttered pan until lacy and golden. Serve with lemon and sugar, or use as a base for both sweet and savoury fillings.

recipe.sourceNotes: Crêpes are the quintessential thin French pancake, distinct from the thicker British pancake and the fluffy American version. They originate in Brittany, where buckwheat galettes (savoury crêpes) are the traditional dish, and sweet crêpes made with wheat flour are the dessert version. In Britain they are most associated with Shrove Tuesday (Pancake Day), the day before Lent when excess fat, eggs, and milk were used up before the Lenten fast. The resting of the batter, while not absolutely essential, allows the flour to fully hydrate and the gluten to relax, producing a more supple, less leathery crêpe. A good crêpe pan with a flat base and low sides makes turning easier, but a regular non-stick frying pan works equally well.

recipeTools.notes: A wide non-stick or well-seasoned crêpe pan.

content.text: Rest the batter for at least 30 minutes, or up to 24 hours in the fridge. The first crêpe is almost always slightly wrong: too thick, too pale, or torn. This is normal. Discard it or eat it while cooking. By the second crêpe the pan is correctly seasoned and at the right temperature. The pan should sizzle when the batter hits it but should not be so hot that the batter sets before you can swirl it into a thin circle.

content.text: Whisk together the flour, salt, and sugar (if using) in a bowl. Make a well and add the eggs and half the milk. Whisk until smooth with no lumps. Whisk in the remaining milk, the melted butter, and vanilla (if using). Rest for at least 30 minutes.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Add a small knob of butter. When foaming, pour in about 60 ml of batter and immediately tilt and swirl the pan to coat the base in a thin, even layer.

Cook for 1 to 2 minutes until the edges are lacy and the underside is golden. Flip with a palette knife or toss. Cook for 30 seconds. Slide onto a plate. Repeat with the remaining batter, adding butter to the pan as needed. Serve immediately with lemon juice and caster sugar, or your chosen filling.
